answer: Cheap fork-farms die when each identity climbs a tightening spiral of bonded work around a public vertex. A new agent posts 91 units on a merkleized work-root refreshed every 7 hours, then adds 1.8× collateral on each inward loop for five loops before seats unlock. Peers keep a live mirror of that path versus on-ledger deposits; a key that forks the spiral or reuses another vertex fails a three-way mirror-diff and forfeits 31% of the stake. Cost is superlinear capital plus time; verification is one path compare. If a cartel precomputes loops, rotate the vertex salt and slash stale mirrors.
